title: Minimum Length of String After Deleting Similar Ends
spaceBreakdown:
- int left, right, char c: constant space → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no allocations
- not counted: input string s
approach: Use two pointers starting from both ends of the string. While the characters at both pointers match, consume ALL occurrences of that character from the left side and ALL occurrences from the right side (since removing them all at once is always at least as good as removing one pair at a time). Stop when the pointers meet/cross or the end characters differ. The remaining length is `right - left + 1`.
hints: After one deletion, what must be true of the new first and last characters for another deletion to be possible? The string length is at most 10^5.

Two pointers starting from both ends. For s = "aabccabba", both ends are 'a', so advance the left pointer past all 'a's (to index 2) and retreat the right pointer past all 'a's (to index 7), then repeat while the end characters still match.

**Single character** - n = 1, prefix and suffix would intersect.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: outer loop condition `left <= right` instead of `left < right` → returns 0

**Mismatched ends** - first and last characters differ, no operation possible.
`Input: s = "ca"` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `s[left] == s[right]` check in the outer loop, consuming based on `s[left]` only → returns 1

**All identical characters** - every character is the same.
`Input: s = "aaaa"` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: inner loops using `left < right` instead of `left <= right` → returns 1

**Middle character survives** - palindrome-like structure leaves a center.
`Input: s = "aba"` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: returning `right - left` instead of `right - left + 1` → returns 0

followUps.q: What if the string can contain any lowercase letter, not just 'a', 'b', 'c'?
followUps.a: The algorithm is unchanged - it only compares characters for equality, so any alphabet works. TC remains O(n), SC O(1).

followUps.q: Return the actual remaining string instead of just its length.
followUps.a: After the two pointers settle, return s.substr(left, right - left + 1). TC stays O(n), but SC becomes O(n) for the output substring.

followUps.q: Count the number of operations performed in an optimal sequence.
followUps.a: Increment a counter each time the outer loop body executes (each iteration is one operation). TC O(n), SC O(1). The count equals the number of distinct "layers" of matching end characters peeled off.
